concept.name: Restaking
concept.definition: Restaking is the reuse of already-staked ETH or liquid staking tokens as cryptoeconomic security for additional services (Actively/Autonomously Verifiable Services, AVSs), letting those services borrow Ethereum's trust while stakers earn extra rewards and accept extra slashing conditions.
concept.intuition: It is posting the same collateral as bail for multiple jobs at once: more income from one deposit, but any job can trigger forfeiture of the shared stake.
concept.mechanics: On EigenLayer, stakers deposit native ETH or LSTs into restaking contracts and delegate to operators who run AVS software (oracles, bridges, data-availability layers). AVSs pay rewards to operators and stakers for correct service and can slash the restaked stake if commitments are broken — extending Ethereum-grade economic security without each service bootstrapping its own validator set.
concept.failure_modes: Stacked slashing conditions mean a bug or dispute in any single AVS can destroy stake that also secures others; leverage-like recursive restaking (LSTs used as collateral to restake) creates contagion paths where one depeg or slash cascades across services.
concept.misconceptions: Restaking does not create new security from nothing — it re-hypothecates the same stake, so total security is only as strong as the weakest slashing regime in the stack. Extra yield is compensation for extra slashing risk, not free return.
concept.example: A staker restakes 32 ETH worth of stETH on EigenLayer and delegates to an operator serving a data-availability AVS; they earn Ethereum staking rewards plus AVS rewards, but an AVS slashing event can burn the same stake backing both.
